worksheet.title: Growing Patterns
worksheet.subtitle: Patterns with three parts
worksheet.learning_goal: I can read a three-part pattern and keep it going.

parts.title: Some patterns have three parts
parts.text: This pattern repeats three shapes: triangle, square, circle. Read it out loud to hear how it repeats.

parts.title: Watch Bit — ▲ ■ ● ▲ ■ ● …
parts.note: It goes triangle, square, circle — then starts again. The next one is ▲.

parts.title: Draw what comes next
parts.prompt: Read the three-part pattern, then draw the next shape in the dashed box.

parts.title: Draw the next TWO
parts.prompt: Keep this pattern going. Draw the next two shapes in the dashed boxes.

parts.title: You try — make your own
parts.prompt: Pick two or three shapes (● ▲ ■ ★) and draw your own pattern that repeats.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: When you know a pattern, you can keep it going as long as you like. Computers use patterns to repeat steps again and again.

parts.title: What this worksheet teaches
parts.text: Children read a three-part repeating pattern, continue it by one and by two shapes, and make their own. Predicting more than one step ahead is a first thinking-skill behind coding. No coding experience needed.

parts.title: Before you start (no computer needed)
parts.text: No computer — paper and a pencil or crayon. You read each prompt aloud; the child draws the shapes. Optional: pattern blocks or coloured beads to build patterns by hand first.

parts.title: How to lead it (about 15 minutes)
text: 1. Show them (you do). Say the three-part pattern aloud — "triangle, square, circle…" The next is a triangle.
2. Do one together. Exercise 1 — circle, square, star, repeating; the next is a circle.
3. Let them try. Children predict the next TWO in Exercise 2, then make their own in Exercise 3.

parts.title: Answer key (these are the verified correct answers)
text: Exercise 1 — circle, square, star, circle, square, star → next is a circle.
Exercise 2 — triangle, circle, triangle, circle, triangle → the next two are circle then triangle.
Exercise 3 — any pattern that truly repeats is correct (e.g. star, circle, star, circle…).

parts.title: If children get stuck — and ways to adjust
text: Watch for (Ex 2): drawing only one shape. Point to both dashed boxes.
Make it easier: do two-part patterns first, then add the third shape.
Make it harder: ask the child to read their own pattern aloud and continue it two more shapes.
Make it active: stomp–clap–jump, stomp–clap–jump and continue it together.

parts.title: Ontario Kindergarten link (official wording)
text: Problem Solving and Innovating — children read, extend, and create repeating patterns.
In plain terms: reading a longer repeating pattern, continuing it, and making one.
No reading is needed from the child — you read each prompt aloud; the child answers by drawing or circling.

parts.title: You'll know it worked when
parts.text: The child continues a three-part pattern correctly, draws two correct shapes in Exercise 2, and makes a pattern in Exercise 3 that truly repeats.
